answer: Escrowed Reputation Decay**: Each identity escrows a marble of compute credit, forfeited if its reviews diverge from the consensus record. Reputation accrues slowly and decays when idle, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must sustain genuine activity to earn trust. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the escrow plus the compute to simulate real work across a canyon of time; a crystal of honest history is cheaper to keep than to fake.
